=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: _cluster_has_only_fixed_markers at line 295-297, called by _recheck_cluster at line 522
  Problem: _cluster_has_only_fixed_markers inspects only pre_existing_statuses (looking for "fixed_by_resolver" without "unchanged") and ignores whether the cluster also carries FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1 markers. _recheck_cluster calls it as the very first check and returns resolved=True when it passes, short-circuiting all quarantine re-evaluation.
  Why it fails at runtime: A cluster that contains both a fixed_by_resolver PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1 marker from one run and a FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1 marker from another run within the same 24h lookback window will be classified as "resolved — close when observed again." The existing tracker issue will be closed or creation will be suppressed, even though the fingerprint is still actively quarantined and the drift has not been verified against the merged PR diff. The quarantine marker is the authoritative signal that the verifier is still hitting and suppressing this fingerprint; closing the tracker issue on fixed_by_resolver alone loses that signal.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: _list_recent_runs at lines 300-335
  Problem: The function requests status and conclusion fields in the --json parameter but never filters runs by status == "completed" before enqueueing them for log fetch. Runs with status "in_progress", "queued", or conclusion "failure" will still have _fetch_run_log called on them.
  Why it fails at runtime: This wastes one gh run view --log API call per in-progress or failed run in the 24h window. In-progress runs may return truncated logs that produce incomplete marker data (though this is fail-safe — fewer markers means fewer tracker issues, not wrong ones). The practical impact is API quota consumption, not incorrect output.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 295-297 (function `_cluster_has_only_fixed_markers`) and 521-526 (usage in `_recheck_cluster`)
  Problem: `_cluster_has_only_fixed_markers()` only examines `pre_existing_statuses` and ignores whether the cluster also contains `FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1` markers. In `_recheck_cluster()`, this check runs BEFORE the quarantine marker check. A cluster with both fixed-by-resolver PRE_EXISTING markers AND FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1 markers will be marked as "resolved" and closed without ever verifying against the merged PR diff.
  Why it fails at runtime: A persistent drift that was quarantined (indicating ongoing active drift) can be incorrectly closed if any recent run reported `fixed_by_resolver`, even though the quarantined marker proves the drift is still being hit.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 300-330 (function `_list_recent_runs`)
  Problem: The function requests `status` and `conclusion` fields from the GitHub API but never uses them to filter runs. Only `created_at` / cutoff time filtering is applied.
  Why it fails at runtime: In-progress, queued, or failed runs can be included in the selected runs list, triggering unnecessary log fetches that waste API quota and potentially produce incomplete or misleading marker data.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 466-480 (function `_fetch_pr_files`)
  Problem: The function returns `None` on any GitHub API error (network, rate limit, transient failure) without any retry logic. The caller treats `None` as "diff unavailable" and marks the cluster recheck as inconclusive.
  Why it fails at runtime: A brief network hiccup or rate-limit throttle can leave a genuine persistent drift cluster open with an inconclusive note, when a simple retry seconds later would succeed.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: _cluster_has_only_fixed_markers() (~lines 297-302) and the early return in _recheck_cluster() (~lines 313-318)
  Problem: The helper returns True for any cluster whose pre_existing_statuses contain only "fixed_by_resolver" (no "unchanged"). _recheck_cluster calls it first and short-circuits to resolved=True without inspecting any FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1 markers that may also be present in the same cluster.
  Why it fails at runtime: A fingerprint that is still being actively quarantined (producing a QUARANTINED_V1 marker in recent runs) alongside fixed_by_resolver markers will cause the tracker issue to be closed or creation suppressed, silently dropping persistent drift from the audit. The later quarantine-specific path and PR-diff recheck are unreachable. Matches consensus findings across multiple reviewers.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: _list_recent_runs() (~lines 307-335)
  Problem: The function requests status/conclusion fields but never filters on status == "completed" (or any conclusion) before adding runs to the selected list.
  Why it fails at runtime: In-progress, queued, or cancelled review_autofix runs can be fetched, producing partial logs (or fetch failures), spurious warnings, and inflated/skewed cluster counts in tracker issues. The audit’s 24-hour window makes this likely on a busy repo.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: _fetch_pr_files() (~lines 440-460) and the handling of None return in _recheck_cluster() / main()
  Problem: Transient GH API errors (rate limit, network, 5xx) cause _fetch_pr_files to return None immediately; the caller marks the recheck “inconclusive” and leaves the tracker open with a generic note. No retry/backoff is present.
  Why it fails at runtime: A one-off API blip during PR-files pagination leaves a real persistent-drift cluster open indefinitely with “recheck inconclusive — PR #N diff unavailable”. Matches a consensus finding.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
